title: AWS AppSync Events with an AWS Lambda OnPublish handler
description: Validate and enrich events in an AWS Lambda function before AWS AppSync Events delivers them to WebSocket subscribers.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: This pattern deploys an AWS AppSync Events API with a direct Lambda integration on the `notifications` channel namespace. Every event published to a `notifications/...` channel goes to an AWS Lambda function (`REQUEST_RESPONSE`) before AppSync broadcasts it to WebSocket subscribers. The function adds `processedAt`, `enriched` and `messageId` fields, and returns an error for a payload that isn't a JSON object.
Use the same hook to validate payloads, redact personal data or add data from another source. A second namespace, `alerts`, has no handler, so you can compare intercepted and plain delivery.
Publishers and subscribers authenticate with an API key that the stack creates with a 365-day expiry. The stack doesn't output the key, so read it with `aws appsync list-api-keys`.

bullets.text: Direct Lambda integration for AWS AppSync Events

text: Subscribe to /notifications/* in the Pub/Sub Editor of the AWS AppSync console, then publish an event to notifications/general with the HTTP endpoint and the API key. The event arrives with the fields the function added. See the README in the GitHub repo for the commands.
Delete the log group that AWS AppSync creates outside the stack: aws logs delete-log-group --log-group-name /aws/appsync/apis/<ApiId>
